item.title: 💗 Your job application was going well, but the company suddenly put the position
item.description:
💗 Your job application was going well, but the company suddenly put the position “on hold.”

What does that mean? 👀

A hiring hold happens when a company temporarily pauses recruitment for a position, sometimes even after interviews have started.

There are several possible reasons:

• Budget changes: The company needs to review spending or secure additional hiring approval.

• Changing priorities: The team may be reconsidering the role, its responsibilities or the experience required.

• Internal delays: Decision-makers may need more time to agree on the next steps.

Does this mean you've been rejected?

Not necessarily! The company might resume hiring later, adjust the position or eventually cancel it.

If you're already in the interview process, it's reasonable to ask whether there's an expected timeline and if you'll remain under consideration when hiring resumes.

One important reminder: A hiring hold isn't a job offer or a guaranteed rejection. If there's no confirmed timeline, keep exploring other opportunities.

item.title: 💗 What's the difference between “required” and “preferred” skills in a job descr
item.description:
💗 What's the difference between “required” and “preferred” skills in a job description? 👀

» Required skills are the qualifications a company considers essential for the position.

» Preferred skills are additional qualifications that could strengthen your application, but aren't necessarily mandatory.

So if you meet the core requirements but you're missing a few preferred skills, the role may still be worth applying for.

The key is understanding which qualifications are essential and which are simply nice to have.

item.title: 💗 Quick reminder for Web3 job seekers! 👀 You don't need to meet every single req
item.description:
💗 Quick reminder for Web3 job seekers! 👀

You don't need to meet every single requirement in a job description to consider applying.

Some requirements are essential, while others describe the company's ideal candidate.

Focus on whether you can handle the core responsibilities, meet the mandatory requirements and demonstrate relevant experience.

Don't reject yourself from an opportunity before the hiring team has even reviewed your application!

item.title: 💗 A quick resume check before your next application: Open your resume and look a
item.description:
💗 A quick resume check before your next application:

Open your resume and look at the first few lines.

Can someone understand what kind of work you've done and what skills you bring without reading the entire document?

If not, consider making your most relevant experience easier to find.

Recruiters shouldn't have to guess what you're good at.
